cards.title: Germany pledges fresh Ukraine aid as Russia escalates attacks
cards.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced more than €1.3 billion in aid during a Kyiv visit as Russia intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities.
detail: The Associated Press reported that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced a package worth more than €1.3 billion during a Sunday visit to Kyiv. About €1 billion is military aid, including long-range weapons, combat drones and satellite technology; another €350 million is for energy repairs and generators ahead of winter.

The package matters because it links immediate air-defence and strike capacity to the seasonal infrastructure problem. Ukraine is entering another winter with energy systems exposed, while Germany is also backing joint counter-drone production.

AP reported that Ukraine and Germany signed 15 agreements worth more than €8.5 billion, mostly on security cooperation, weapons production and procurement. The aid announcement is verified; its battlefield effect and delivery schedule are not yet established.

Kyiv also said Washington had proposed technical-level trilateral talks with Russia by the end of October. Russia’s response, the delivery timetable and the durability of the diplomatic track remain open.
